vectors.normative_sentence: A conformance artifact pack MUST identify this document as the repository-authoritative ESRM v0.1 baseline for Sections 22 through 48.
A conformance artifact pack MUST distinguish NORMATIVE text from NON-NORMATIVE text.
A conformance artifact pack MUST NOT treat examples, rationale, or implementation notes as normative requirements.
A conformance artifact pack MUST NOT claim ESRM conformance before independent audit and before both Rust and Go implementations pass the finalized corpus.
An implementation MUST accept each artifact as an exact finite byte sequence before any decoding.
An implementation MUST record raw_byte_length before JSON parsing.
An implementation MUST record raw_sha256 as SHA-256 over the exact finite byte sequence.
An implementation MUST NOT normalize Unicode before raw_sha256 is recorded.
An implementation MUST NOT translate CRLF, CR, or LF before raw_sha256 is recorded.
An implementation MUST NOT infer a character encoding other than UTF-8.
After raw_sha256 is recorded, JSON artifacts MUST decode as valid UTF-8.
JSON artifacts MUST contain exactly one top-level JSON object.
JSON artifacts MUST reject duplicate object member names at every object depth.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT contain a UTF-8 BOM.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT contain leading whitespace before the top-level object.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT contain trailing bytes or trailing whitespace after the top-level object.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT use comments, trailing commas, NaN, Infinity, or implementation-specific JSON extensions.
JSON values MUST satisfy I-JSON constraints before JCS canonicalization.
Numeric values MUST be integers in the inclusive range 0 through 9007199254740991 unless a schema field explicitly forbids numbers entirely.
Numeric-profile enforcement MUST apply recursively inside extension containers.
JSON numbers MUST NOT be negative, fractional, exponential, NaN, or Infinity.
JSON strings MUST NOT contain unpaired surrogate code points.
Canonicalization MUST use RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme after strict intake, I-JSON, schema, semantic, and numeric-profile checks.
Canonical bytes MUST be UTF-8 encoded RFC 8785 JCS output.
An implementation MUST NOT canonicalize invalid JSON or schema-invalid artifacts.
An implementation MUST NOT substitute local member-ordering, whitespace, or number-rendering behavior for RFC 8785 JCS.
Every governed artifact MUST declare artifact_type using the closed artifact-type registry.
Every governed artifact MUST declare domain using the closed domain registry.
Every governed artifact MUST include raw_sha256 and canonical_sha256 when the artifact is JSON-governed.
Registry values MUST NOT accept aliases, case variants, prefixes, or suffixes.
A domain commitment MUST NOT be inferred from file path, branch name, repository name, or caller identity.
The artifact-type registry MUST be closed for ESRM v0.1.
The domain registry MUST be closed for ESRM v0.1.
The registry MUST define a bijection check between schema-governed artifact types and schema identifiers.
Implementations MUST NOT dynamically add artifact types or domains during conformance execution.
`critical_extensions` MUST be an array when present.
Each critical extension entry MUST contain `extension_id`, `extension_version`, `critical`, and `payload`.
`critical` MUST be true for every critical extension entry.
`extension_id` MUST match `^esrm\.[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$`.
An artifact MUST contain no more than 16 critical extension entries.
Each serialized critical extension payload MUST be no larger than 8192 bytes.
Unknown critical extension identifiers MUST NOT be ignored.
Extension containers MUST NOT bypass recursive numeric-profile enforcement.
A raw artifact MUST be no larger than 1048576 bytes.
A parsed JSON artifact MUST have maximum nesting depth no greater than 32.
A parsed JSON artifact MUST have no more than 4096 object members total.
A parsed JSON artifact MUST have no array longer than 1024 elements.
Implementations MUST NOT continue parsing after a resource limit is exceeded.

A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `transition_id`, `artifact_type`, `domain`, `schema_version`, `input_commitments`, `output_commitments`, `operation_label`, `raw_sha256`, and `canonical_sha256`.
`input_commitments` and `output_commitments` MUST contain unique commitment strings sorted by bytewise ASCII order.
`operation_label` MUST match `^esrm\.[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$`.
A transition artifact MUST NOT contain lifecycle-state fields in ESRM v0.1 canonical raw-byte conformance.
A transition artifact MUST NOT imply mutation of an input artifact.
A `proofrail.signature` artifact MUST bind exactly one `subject_canonical_sha256`.
The crypto suite MUST be `PR-ESRM-JCS-SHA256-ED25519-v1`.
Hash commitments MUST use SHA-256 encoded as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
Signature mode MUST be pure Ed25519 per RFC 8032.
`signature_b64u` MUST decode to exactly 64 bytes using unpadded base64url.
`public_key_b64u` MUST decode to exactly 32 bytes using unpadded base64url.
Permissive Base64 decoding MUST NOT be used.
Invalid point encodings and noncanonical signature scalars MUST be rejected.
Signature artifacts MUST NOT contain private keys, bearer tokens, cookies, or secret headers.
A signature artifact MUST prove only that the subject commitment was signed by the declared public key.
Authority to produce an external effect MUST require a separate authority artifact outside this raw-byte conformance phase.
A valid signature MUST NOT be treated as permission to execute an action.
A signature verifier MUST NOT choose an implicit trust root.
Reconciliation claims MUST be represented as deterministic relations between input commitments and output commitments.
A reconciliation relation MUST preserve all input commitments.
Reconciliation MUST NOT erase, rewrite, or mutate a prior commitment.
Inconclusive reconciliation MUST NOT be reported as success.
Consumption records MUST be append-only commitment records.
A consumed authority commitment MUST remain visible to later verification.
A consumed authority commitment MUST NOT be returned to an unconsumed state.
Replay of a consumed commitment MUST NOT be accepted as fresh authority.
External-effect claims MUST identify the exact boundary where local verification ends and external provider state begins.
Ambiguous external-effect outcomes MUST be recorded as ambiguous.
An implementation MUST NOT convert an ambiguous external outcome into success without independent observation.
Raw-byte conformance MUST NOT claim production exactly-once external execution.
A conformance implementation MUST expose independent parse, schema, semantic, canonicalization, signature, and commitment checks.
A conformance result MUST include rejection_stage and reason_code for every negative vector.
A conformance implementation MUST NOT hide parser failures behind a generic failure code.
Rejection precedence MUST be deterministic.

Rejection precedence MUST be raw_byte_intake, resource_limit, utf8_decode, json_parse, duplicate_member, schema_validation, registry_lookup, semantic_validation, canonicalization, commitment_validation, signature_validation, claim_boundary.
Implementations MUST NOT report a later-stage rejection when an earlier-stage rejection applies.
The corpus manifest MUST enumerate every vector file by relative path, raw byte length, and SHA-256.
Every vector MUST list the normative requirement IDs it covers.
Every negative vector MUST list expected rejection_stage and reason_code.
Vector files MUST NOT depend on absolute host paths, local usernames, environment variables, or wall-clock time.
Generated corpus families MUST declare generator_id, generator_version, PRNG algorithm, seed, case ordering, and reproduction command.
The PRNG algorithm for generated ESRM v0.1 vectors MUST be ChaCha20 with a 256-bit seed encoded as 64 lowercase hex characters.
Case ordering MUST be lexicographic by vector_id after generation.
Corpus generation MUST NOT read host time, network state, process ID, or random device state after the declared seed is set.
The file-hash manifest MUST enumerate every governed file except itself.
The file-hash manifest exclusion MUST be explicit.
The file-hash manifest SHA-256 MUST be recorded in a separate release-root record or immutable git commit.
A file-hash manifest MUST NOT claim to contain its own hash unless a separate self-reference construction is specified.
JSON Schemas MUST use Draft 2020-12.
JSON Schemas MUST contain explicit `$schema` and stable `$id` fields.
JSON Schemas MUST set `additionalProperties` to false for governed artifacts.
JSON Schema `format` assertions MUST NOT be normative for ESRM v0.1 conformance.
Implementations MUST NOT rely on validator-specific `format` behavior for pass/fail decisions.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate parsing implementations.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate JCS canonicalization implementations.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate base64url implementations.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate Ed25519 verification implementations.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate JSON Schema validation implementations.
Rust and Go tracks MUST use separate SHA-256 or commitment implementations.
A Rust track MUST NOT call a Go validator.
A Go track MUST NOT call a Rust validator.
Either track MUST NOT shell out to the other track for conformance decisions.
Validation output MUST distinguish parse validation, schema validation, semantic validation, canonicalization validation, signature validation, commitment validation, and end-to-end conformance.
Validation output MUST report uncovered requirements.
Validation output MUST report unresolved ambiguities.
Validation output MUST NOT claim conformance from artifact parse success alone.
Implementation work MUST NOT begin until this artifact pack has been independently audited.
A release candidate MUST include normative source, registries, schemas, coverage inventory, dependency report, risk register, validation results, file-hash manifest, and release-root record.
A release candidate MUST NOT merge without explicit operator direction.
The artifact pack MUST record deviations from supplied ESRM language.
Missing source language MUST be reported as an unresolved evidence gap.
An implementation MUST NOT silently resolve a contradiction by local choice.
Every unresolved ambiguity MUST have a stable ambiguity ID.
Every ambiguity record MUST list affected vector families.
Affected vector families MUST be stopped when implementation would require inventing protocol semantics.
A stopped vector family MUST NOT be counted as passed conformance.
This phase MUST state `NO CLAIM OF CONFORMANCE` in its validation summary.
This phase MUST state that Rust and Go implementations have not begun.
This phase MUST NOT claim lifecycle, dispatch, reconciliation, settlement, or recovery engine behavior.
